requirements.text: Make sure their employee profile reflects remote-based work location
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_profile WHERE hr_profile_id = 19 AND location_type = 'Remote'
assumptions: Angela Brooks is user 19 (the only user of that name; position Administration) with hr_profile 19
the seed's location_type values are Hotdesk, Office Based and Remote; remote-based work is Remote
the seed has Office Based on her profile

requirements.text: that this change is properly tracked for HR follow-up ... handled as a standard workforce administration change and documented appropriately as Work Location Update

cells.hr_service: IN (SELECT hr_service_id FROM hr_service WHERE active = 1)

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id = 61 AND opened_for = 19 AND opened_by = 41 AND hr_service IN (SELECT hr_service_id FROM hr_service WHERE active = 1) AND coe_type = 'Workforce Administration' AND priority = 'high' AND short_description LIKE '%Work Location Update%'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest hr_case_id in the seed is 60); the only case the task creates
opened_for is Angela Brooks's hr_profile 19 (opened_for references hr_profile)
opened_by is the requester per policy 3.1: the acting user Scott Mitchell, hr_profile 41
the request names no service and no service is named Work Location Update; policy 3.1 makes an active hr_service a mandatory input, so any active service passes
a standard workforce administration change gives coe_type Workforce Administration
'documented as Work Location Update' is read as the case's description containing that phrase
'very urgent' fixes a priority above the policy's moderate default but not which level; high kept from the benchmark check
disagreement: opened_by: A 41, B untested; chose 41 because policy 3.1 defines opened_by as the requester, here the acting user Scott Mitchell (hr_profile 41); the request names no other requester

disagreement: hr_service: A any active service, B untested; chose any active service because policy 3.1 makes an active hr_service a mandatory input on a new case, while the request names none, so no single service can be required

requirements.text: the employee is formally notified about the update
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE notification_id = 61 AND hr_case_id = 61 AND email = 'angela.brooks@phillips-jones.com' AND type = 'update' AND status = 'ready'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest notification_id in the seed is 60); the only notification the task creates
the notification belongs to the new case 61
angela.brooks@phillips-jones.com is her user email; the request does not say which address, kept from the benchmark check
type update matches 'notified about the update'
status ready kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy

notes:
disagreement: value: the case's opened_by: one pass tests 41, the other leaves it untested; kept 41 because policy 3.1 makes opened_by the requester, the acting user (logged in the requirement).
disagreement: value: the case's hr_service: one pass requires any active service, the other leaves it untested; kept the predicate because policy 3.1 makes an active service mandatory on a new case (logged in the requirement).
The two passes otherwise agree on every requirement, id, cell and disposition (all three checks kept); their texts and assumptions differ in wording only.
The profile check returns location_type rather than a count; it is carried as a count of hr_profile 19 with location_type Remote. Its description's 'Office Based' is the seed value, not the target; its expected value Remote is what the request states.
'Tracked for HR follow-up' and 'documented as Work Location Update so HR can review it later' are read as the one HR case; the request does not ask for a separate fulfilment task, although a task-creation tool is listed, and the policy has tasks generated when a case starts work.
Every seed notification is addressed to a profile's personal email, while the benchmark notifies Angela Brooks's user email; the request only says the employee is notified, so the benchmark's address is kept, and a notification to her personal address would fail it.
The case's status and short-description template are not tested: the policy's default state 'new' is not a status this database uses, and the 'Service: , Subject: , Detail: ' template and 30-120 character limit are policy format rules the benchmark does not test.
The acting user Scott Mitchell holds the admin role, which the policy says must not perform routine HR case work; the request and the benchmark's checks expect the work, so the requirements follow them.
